The wild mollies from Central America have always been, and will remain, an enigma for generations of scientists. In each brook the fish look somewhat different. Within every population there are also differently shaped males: small, slender, early-ripening males, large, deep-bodied, late-ripening males, and males somewhere in between. It is therefore not certain whether these fish, bred in Southeast Asia, really belong to the species P. mexicana, to P. sphenops or to P. limantouri. From a practical point of view, however, these questions are rather irrelevant.

It is very important always to add the term "Campeche", the locality where the initial stock was collected, since otherwise unwanted crosses cannot be excluded.

These wild-type mollies are a real challenge for hobby breeders. In contrast to Black Mollies, Silver Mollies and so on, the young fish grow extremely slowly. The adult fish, however, reward the keeper with lively behaviour and brilliant colours. Their ability to change colour is remarkable: within seconds the males change from a silvery neutral pattern to a blue-black display pattern. If the fish are disturbed, they can turn pale in an instant. After only a few days of settling in, however, they are hardly disturbed any more.
